newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Rebels surrender in Indonesia's Irian Jaya -agency.
newsitem.headline: Rebels surrender in Indonesia's Irian Jaya -agency.

text.p: Twelve members of a separatist group in Indonesia's remote Irian Jaya province have surrendered to authorities along with their families, the official Antara news agency reported on Friday.

Antara quoted Irian Jaya military spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Maulud Hidayat as saying the rebels, led by Martinus Okayanum, surrendered to the military in Merauke regency on Wednesday along with their family members.

Antara quoted the spokesman as saying Okayanum and his group, who lived near the border with Papua New Guinea, decided to surrender after learning that other members of the separatist movement who had done so were treated humanely and given assistance by the local administration to start a new life.
Hidayat was quoted as saying that no punishment would be imposed on the rebels and that more and more members of the separatist movement had decided to return to society.

Antara said Okayanum's group was the second batch of rebels to surrender to the military in less than one month. On May 25, 72 members of the separatist movement led by Willem Onde surrendered to the military and gave up 46 guns.
Irian Jaya, on the western half of New Guinea island, is home to the Free Papua Movement (OPM), which has waged a sporadic battle against Indonesian rule.
